def:ncg-grand-tensor.title: Finite Renewal Grand Tensor
def:ncg-grand-tensor.note: Encoded. `GrandTensor` bundles the complete finite-future predictive law (whose quotient is the future-minimal carrier Z^min = PredictiveSystem.MinimalCarrier) with a represented generator family gen : Γ → Matrix M M ℂ on a finite support-minimal carrier; from it are derived the represented history algebra A^hist = StarAlgebra.adjoin ℂ (range gen) (eq:ncg-history-algebra), the represented word operators [w] (wordOp, multiplicative under concatenation), the normalized regular trace τ_reg = normalizedRegularTrace A^hist (eq:ncg-grand-regular-trace), the word-Gram kernel K_X(v,w) = τ_reg([v]^*[w]) (wordGram, eq:ncg-word-gram) and its depth-r layers K_{X,r} (wordGramLevel). Disclosed: the tomographic construction of the generator family from the intervention tables is not formalized (gen is data), and positivity of the Gram kernel is not proved (it is a remark in the paper, not part of the definition).

thm:summary-affinity.note: Proved (summary form of thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge plus cor:supp-faithful-modular, both proved records; same Lean). def:finite-real-differential.title: Finite real differential datum

thm:finite-Hodge-Dirac.title: Finite Hodge--Dirac spectral triple
thm:finite-Hodge-Dirac.note: Relabelled successor of the removed proved record thm:finite-spectralization; its Lean applies verbatim. Proved in orthonormal coordinates (Packet): D = fromBlocks 0 d^H d 0 Hermitian (dirac_isHermitian) and odd, D gamma = -gamma D (dirac_odd); J = j o conj with J^2 = I (realMatrix_sq), JD = DJ (realMatrix_intertwines_dirac), J gamma = gamma J (realMatrix_commutes_grading), i.e. the KO-dimension-0 signs; opposite representation J pi(b^*) J^{-1} = R_b (+) rho(b) (realMatrix_implements_opposite); order zero and first order (order_zero, first_order); the commutator block formula eq:finite-commutator (dirac_commutator_formula); ||[D,pi(a)]|| = ||B_a|| for a = a^* (commutator_norm_eq_B, via norm_offDiagonal); the kernel clause of eq:finite-Lip follows by combining commutator_norm_eq_B with B_eq_zero_iff_partialVector_eq_zero (B_a = 0 iff the source-minimal differential vector, i.e. partial a, vanishes). Compact resolvent and boundedness of [D,pi(a)] are automatic in finite dimension. Disclosed (as for the predecessor): the Leibniz block identity, right-linearity of B_a and the reversal intertwining are structure fields of Packet; faithfulness of pi and unitarity of the matrix j are not stated; the new explicit even-grading axioms gamma^* = gamma, gamma^2 = I, [gamma, pi(a)] = 0 hold by the block definitions grading = fromBlocks 1 0 0 (-1), representation = fromBlocks (left0 a) 0 0 (left1 a) but are not separate lemmas.

prop:finite-CQMS.note: Proved, with the following disclosed scoping. def:supp-renewal-graph.title: Stationary finite Markov graph
def:supp-renewal-graph.note: Bundled structure StationaryRenewalGraph V: masses m_x > 0 with sum 1, rates k_xy >= 0 for x != y (diagonal normalized to 0, since the generator sum over y != x ignores it), the mass-stationarity equation sum_y (q_xy - q_yx) = 0 for q = m k, and connectedness (ConductanceConnected) of the positive support of c = (q+q^T)/2. thm:supp-A3-finite.title: $A_3$ Hodge identities and smooth-function consistency
thm:supp-A3-finite.note: Proved. All four clauses on the actual finite periodic A3 graph (vertices V_h = h Lambda/Lambda as Fin 3 -> ZMod d, mesh h = 1/d, rates 1/(8h^2), masses h^3, root steps reduced modulo the period): (i) eq:supp-A3-Lip, L_h(f)^2 = max_x (1/(8h^2)) sum_alpha |f(x+h alpha)-f(x)|^2 (graphLipschitz_sample_sq_eq, previous pass); (ii) eq:supp-A3-square via the general stationary theorem (previous pass); (iii) NEW eq:supp-A3-Lip-convergence with the explicit constant C_{A3} = 4 + sum_i |b_i| = 4 + 3 sqrt 2: graphLipschitz_rate shows |L_h(F|V_h) - sup_M |grad F|| <= (4 + sum_i |b_i|) M_2 h for every lattice-periodic C^1 field F whose gradient is M_2-Lipschitz (sup_M |grad F| rendered as sSup of the range of |grad F|; since grad F is periodic this is the L^infinity norm on the torus). Ingredients: first-order Taylor remainder along each root via the mean-value inequality (rootDifference_error_le, |(F(x+h alpha)-F(x))/h - alpha.grad F| <= |alpha|^2 M_2 h = 2 M_2 h), the existing reverse-triangle/tight-frame estimate (sqrt_energy_error_le) giving a pointwise error 4 M_2 h, a mesh-covering lemma (exists_vertex_near: every point of the torus is within h sum_i |b_i| of a vertex after a lattice translation, via floors in the period basis and ZMod.val_intCast) and periodicity of the gradient (gradient_periodic) to compare the max over the mesh with the sup over the torus; (iv) NEW generator clause: tendstoUniformly_generator proves (L_h F)(x) := (1/(8h^2)) sum_alpha (F(x+h alpha)-F(x)) -> (1/2) Delta F uniformly on the torus as h -> 0+ for every lattice-periodic C^2 field (F, DF, D^2F with D^2F continuous; the Hessian is uniformly continuous by periodicity), with Delta F = sum_i D^2F(e_i,e_i); ingredients: uniform second-order Taylor remainder by two one-dimensional mean-value inequalities (second_order_remainder), cancellation of the linear terms (sum of the twelve roots is zero) and the polarized tight-frame identity sum_alpha B(alpha,alpha) = 8 sum_i B(e_i,e_i) for every bilinear form (sum_root_bilinear, lem:supp-A3-frame), giving (h^2/2) 8 Delta F /(8 h^2) = Delta F/2; generator_sample_eq identifies the sampled generator at the vertices with the finite-graph generator of eq:supp-A3-square applied to F|V_h. Renderings disclosed: the paper's C^2 norm enters the rate only through the Lipschitz constant of grad F, so the rate theorem takes that constant M_2 (<= |F|_{C^2}) as hypothesis; the generator limit is proved under C^2 (weaker than the paper's C^4) as uniform convergence without a rate, exactly as the theorem states (the O(h^2 |F|_{C^4}) rate mentioned only in the proof is not formalised).

thm:supp-graph-realization.title: Stationary Markov realization fibre of a metric graph triple

thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge.title: Affinity coordinates for a fixed-traffic Markov fibre
thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge.note: Proved for a real incidence matrix B with the connected-incidence hypotheses Bᵀ1 = 0 and ker Bᵀ = constants (IsConnectedIncidence) and positive conductances: the affinity functional F_α(φ) = Σ c_e log cosh(a₀_e + (Bᵀφ)_e) has a unique mean-zero minimiser φ_α; a_α = a₀ + Bᵀφ_α and j_α = c tanh a_α satisfy B j_α = 0, |j_α| < c, artanh(j_α/c) = a_α, [a_α] = α, and j_α is the unique fibre current of class α; the affinity map 𝔄 : 𝒥(G,c) → H¹(G;ℝ) = ℝ^E / Ran Bᵀ is a bijection (Set.BijOn onto the quotient). Coercivity is proved as F_α(φ) + (Σφ)² → ∞ along the cocompact filter. Not formalised: strict convexity of F_α (uniqueness is derived from the Euler equation plus strict monotonicity of tanh instead) and the smoothness of 𝔄⁻¹ (the word 'diffeomorphism'); the bijection and explicit inverse formulas are proved. thm:supp-current-chain.title: Graph quotients and entropy contraction
thm:supp-current-chain.note: Proved over R for finite oriented graphs (tail/head maps, multi-edges allowed) and a vertex quotient q : V -> V-bar with induced coarse graph in which every fine edge is either mapped to a coarse edge with the quotient endpoints or is internal to a fibre and dropped (VertexQuotient); Q_V, Q_E are the fibre-summation matrices. (i) chain identity d-bar Q_E = Q_V d as a matrix identity, hence Q_E Z(G) <= Z(G-bar); (ii) Q_E Curr(G,c) <= Curr(G-bar, c-bar) with c-bar = Q_E c, under the hypothesis that every coarse edge has a nonempty fibre ('retains every inter-fibre edge class', needed for the strict inequality); (iii) with connected fibres (through internal edges) and retained classes, Q_E : Z(G) -> Z(G-bar) is onto (constructive lift: one representative per coarse edge, divergence completed by internal path flows), so the short sequence is exact and dim ker = dim Z(G) - dim Z(G-bar); with G and G-bar connected and nonempty this is (|E|-|V|+1) - (|E-bar|-|V-bar|+1) via a real Betti-number lemma; (iv) sigma_{G-bar}(Q_E j) <= sigma_G(j) for j in the open polytope with c > 0, via the log-sum inequality (sum_rateDivergence_ge_total) applied to forward/reverse fluxes c +- j on each coarse-edge fibre. It interprets F_{A,mu}(0) as the limit from the negative real axis, whereas Lean evaluates the Stieltjes self-energy at 0 directly; under Q_0 finite the two agree (dominated convergence, |lambda - z|^{-1} <= lambda^{-1} for z < 0), and equality of the two negative-axis limits also follows from the formalised bound (2) with r = |z| -> 0; this limit step is not separately stated in Lean. Proved for the general weakly countably additive measure of def:supp-POVM (PositiveTailMeasure; Stieltjes integrals are Mathlib vector-measure integrals), in the L2 operator norm on Matrix H H C, with F_{A,mu}(z) = A - z - Sigma_mu(z), Q_{>Lambda} = int_{(Lambda,inf)} lambda^{-1} dmu, mu|_{(0,Lambda]} = restriction to Iic Lambda, RG_Lambda(A,mu) = (A - Q_{>Lambda}, mu|_{(0,Lambda]}). (1) eq:supp-memory-static-preserved (dynamicFunction_rg_zero): F_{RG}(0) = F(0) under the hypothesis that lambda^{-1} is mu-integrable, i.e. exactly that the static value F_{A,mu}(0) exists (the paper's implicit assumption; without it both sides are the Lean convention value and the identity is false). (2) eq:supp-memory-screen-error (norm_dynamicFunction_sub_rg_le): for ||z|| <= r < Lambda and z outside [0,inf) (the domain of the Stieltjes self-energy in def:supp-POVM), ||F(z) - F_{RG}(z)|| <= r/(Lambda - r) ||Q_{>Lambda}||, no integrability hypothesis needed; the variant _of_integrable takes instead the integrability of (lambda - z)^{-1}. The analytic core is the positive-weighted operator-norm bound for operator integrals l2_opNorm_integral_le_of_norm_le (||int c dmu|| <= kappa ||int w dmu|| when |c| <= kappa w a.e., w >= 0), proved by scalarising along the sesquilinear complex measures <x, mu(.) y>, dominating their total variation by (t/2)<x,mu x> + (1/(2t))<y,mu y> via the PSD Cauchy-Schwarz inequality posSemidef_norm_sesqForm_le, integrating and optimising in t. (3) eq:supp-memory-semigroup (rg_rg): RG_{Lambda2} o RG_{Lambda1} = RG_{Lambda2} for 0 < Lambda2 <= Lambda1 (head corrections add over the disjoint shells, cutoffs compose). Packaged in memory_rg_semigroup. The finite atomic special case remains in MemoryCutoffSemigroupExact (its scalar tail estimate norm_inv_sub_inv_le is reused).

thm:supp-marked-bundle.note: Proved for an arbitrary group Gamma in the role of G_S = Aut(S) (vertex packets identified with the reference packet, so edge maps are elements of Gamma with U(bar e) = U(e)^{-1} built into backward traversal) on any NCG.Multigraph connected to the base vertex v0. (B1): the walk holonomy (ordered product of edge labels) is multiplicative under concatenation, unital, inverts under reversal and is backtracking invariant, hence is the monodromy homomorphism on pi_1(Gamma, v0) presented as closed walks modulo backtracking; (B2): a frame change g conjugates every loop holonomy by the single element g(v0); (B3): a global marked trivialisation (frame change making every edge map the identity) exists iff all loop holonomies are 1; (B4): two bundle data are gauge equivalent iff their loop holonomies at v0 are conjugate by one element (the clutching classification Hom(pi_1, G_S)/G_S). Reformulation disclosed: pi_1 is presented by closed walks (not as the free group on chords of a spanning tree), so the remark that the bundle is determined by b_1 elements of G_S modulo conjugation is not formalised; compactness of G_S is not used.

cor:supp-twisted-bundle.note: Re-verified against the new statement: the corollary now asserts directly that nontrivial [rho_U] obstructs a global marked trivialization compatible with the edge identifications (no longer phrased through 'flat twisted spectral geometry'). thm:character-holonomy-detection.note: Relabelled from thm:supp-character-shadow; re-verified against the new statement: the converse is now quantified 'for all such graph bundles'. thm:supp-monodromy-descent.title: Exact marked-monodromy descent

def:stable-spin-atlas.title: Compatible stable spin discretization
def:stable-spin-atlas.note: Abstract surrogate encoded (structure CompatibleStableAtlas). Continuum objects replaced as follows: L^2(M; S ⊗ C^2) -> a complex Hilbert space H; D̂ = D ⊗ σ_1 -> an unbounded self-adjoint operator given as SelfAdjointResolventData (a symmetric LinearPMap `op` with, for every non-real z, a bounded two-sided inverse of op − z; isSelfAdjoint_op proves this is self-adjoint in Mathlib's LinearPMap sense, dense_domain that its domain is dense, ofBounded that every bounded self-adjoint operator is an instance); smooth doubled spinors -> a subspace `core` ≤ domain with the field `core_dense` stating that it is a core (graph-dense), which the paper's proof of thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent uses as a known fact about smooth spinors; H^1(M; S ⊗ C^2) -> a Banach space V with a compact linear embedding `sobolev : V → H` (Rellich as a hypothesis); finite Hilbert spaces ℋ_h -> finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces Hn n with self-adjoint stage operators `stage n` (D_h) and linear isometries `embed n` (W_h). (A1)–(A3) are fields verbatim: W_h W_h^* → I strongly; discrete first-order norms with ‖I_h u‖_V ≤ C ‖u‖_{1,h} and ‖I_h u − W_h u‖ ≤ ε_h ‖u‖_{1,h}, ε_h → 0; the assembled graph estimate ‖u‖_{1,h} ≤ C(‖D_h u‖ + ‖u‖); samples S_h ψ of core vectors with W_h S_h ψ → ψ and W_h D_h S_h ψ → D̂ψ. Scoped disclosures: the constants C, ε_h and the discrete norms are required nonnegative; the optional clause on real and grading structures intertwining the reconstructions is not encoded.

thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent.title: Norm-resolvent convergence for compatible stable atlases
thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent.note: Proved in the abstract surrogate of def:stable-spin-atlas (see that record for the object replacements), following the paper's proof step by step: eq:uniform-resolvent-bounds (norm_resolvent_le, for D̂ and for each D_h through ofBounded); strong resolvent convergence W_h(D_h−z)^{-1}W_h^* f → (D̂−z)^{-1} f for every f from (A3) by the core argument (tendsto_embeddedResolvent_core on (D̂−z)(core) via (D_h−z)^{-1}W_h^*(D̂−z)ψ − S_hψ = (D_h−z)^{-1}[W_h^*(D̂ψ − W_hD_hS_hψ) − z W_h^*(ψ − W_hS_hψ)], density of (D̂−z)(core) from the core hypothesis and surjectivity of D̂−z, then the uniform-bound dense-source extension of DenseSourceStrongConvergence); strong convergence of the adjoints via R_h(z)^* = R_h(z̄), R(z)^* = R(z̄) (adjoint_embeddedResolvent, adjoint_resolvent); collective compactness (the Rellich step) from (A1)–(A2), the compact embedding and finite-dimensionality of the stages (collectivelyCompact_embeddedResolvent); norm upgrade by tendsto_operatorNorm_of_collectivelyCompact_of_adjointStrong. Main clause eq:supp-global-norm-resolvent = tendsto_norm_embeddedResolvent_sub for every z with Im z ≠ 0, together with compactness of the limit resolvent. Spectral-projection clause: circleRieszProjection_embeddedResolvent_tendsto gives operator-norm convergence of the Riesz projections of the compressed resolvents on every circle contained in the resolvent set of (D̂−z)^{-1} (isolated bounded-energy clusters of D̂ correspond to such circles under λ ↦ (λ−z)^{-1}; this identification is not formalised). The periodic-extension clause eq:supp-local-norm-resolvent is the same abstract theorem applied to the periodic-extension atlas; the local estimates that supply its (A1)–(A3) are the separate records lem:supp-general-Garding / lem:supp-general-core. Not encoded: retention of real and grading structures.

cor:supp-flat-torus-spin.title: Unconditional periodic flat-spin norm-resolvent convergence
cor:supp-flat-torus-spin.note: Partial: the abstract theorem (compatible stable atlas implies norm-resolvent convergence, tendsto_norm_embeddedResolvent_sub) and the constant-coefficient ingredients are proved: unique species of the frozen Wilson symbol, the frozen discrete Garding bound h1NormSq_le, core consistency of the frozen Wilson operator against the frozen Dirac operator, and the isometric piecewise-constant embedding of periodic grid functions into L^2(T^3) (scalar, three-dimensional). cor:supp-flat-torus-spin.plan: New file OperatorLimits/FlatTorusSpinAtlas.lean. Continuum side on UnitAddTorus (Fin d) with values in EuclideanSpace C (Fin N): D-hat as a Fourier multiplier via mFourierBasis (symbol sum_j c^j 2 pi k_j (x) sigma_1, Hermitian), resolvent multiplier (sigma(k) - z)^{-1} bounded by 1/|Im z|, domain = weighted l^2; trigonometric polynomials as core (truncation of Fourier series converges in graph norm); V = H^1 as the weighted l^2 space with compact embedding (diagonal multiplier (1+|k|^2)^{-1/2} -> 0, compact as a norm limit of finite-rank truncations). cor:supp-compact-spin-image.title: Conditional stable compact-spin approximation
cor:supp-compact-spin-image.note: Assembled in the abstract surrogate with the convergence clause now included. ConvergentMarkedSpinDiscretization renders 'a closed marked Riemannian spin manifold admitting a compatible stable spin discretization with independent metric heads': a CompatibleStableAtlas for the doubled Dirac operator, a compact chain metric space X (the manifold with its geodesic distance) and a MeshSequence of finite endpoint metric heads with positive edge lengths. approximation gives (i) norm-resolvent approximation of the doubled spin operator by the finite stage operators for every non-real z (thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent / thm:compact-spin-main), (ii) exactness of every metric head (pure-state Connes distance = graph shortest-path metric), and (iii) convergence of the independent metric heads: an error sequence → 0 bounds |d_h^met(x,y) − d_g(x,y)| over all vertex pairs (thm:supp-global-metric, clause 3). convergentStableCompactSpinApproximation_forall is the essential-surjectivity clause: supplying such data for every target in a family yields the approximation for every member. toMarkedSpinDiscretization links to the earlier partial structure. con:supp-Naimark-tail.title: Canonical minimal Stieltjes dilation
con:supp-Naimark-tail.note: Construction encoded, with its defining properties proved. Analysis/OperatorMeasureL2Completion.lean builds, for any positive-semidefinite-valued vector measure μ with finite variation (PosOperatorMeasure; PositiveTailMeasure.toPosOperatorMeasure), the pre-Hilbert space PreL2 μ of bounded measurable H-valued functions with the semi-inner product ⟨f,g⟩_μ = ∫⟨f, dμ g⟩ (form; on indicators it is the paper's ∑⟨ξ_j, μ(E_j ∩ F_k) η_k⟩, form_indicator_const; positivity for simple functions by SimpleFunc.induction and for bounded measurable functions by dominated convergence, re_form_self_nonneg), the Hilbert space K_μ = L2 μ := Completion (SeparationQuotient (PreL2 μ)) (quotient by the null space, completed) with dense embedding L2.mk, the bounded multipliers L2.mul g (‖g f‖_μ ≤ sup|g| ‖f‖_μ from positivity applied to √(sup|g|²−|g|²) f; multiplicative, unital, additive, adjoint = conj), the projection-valued measure P_μ(E) = L2.proj (multiplication by 1_E: self-adjoint idempotents, P(E∩F)=P(E)P(F), P(univ)=1, finitely additive, strongly σ-additive hasSum_proj), and V_μ ξ = [1 ξ] = L2.embed with B_μ = V_μ^* (compressB). The unbounded operator C_μ = ∫λ dP_μ is not defined as a LinearPMap (no spectral theorem in Mathlib); it is represented by its bounded functional calculus: resolventOp z = multiplication by (λ−z)^{-1} (the resolvent (C_μ−z)^{-1}, z ∉ [0,∞)) and heatOp t = multiplication by e^{-tλ} (e^{-tC_μ}); these multipliers are set to 0 on the μ-null set (−∞,0] so that they are bounded. Disclosed surrogate: the pre-Hilbert space uses bounded measurable functions instead of simple functions (the simple functions are dense in it, mk_mem_closure_sourceSpan), which yields the same completion.

def:supp-rational-Hermitian.title: Normalized rational Hermitian dynamic function
def:supp-rational-Hermitian.note: Encoded: Q is represented by its Hermitian Laurent coefficients M_n at infinity (eq:supp-rational-Laurent; Q(z-bar)^* = Q(z) is coeff_symmetric, Q(infinity)=0 is strict properness of the expansion) with rationality encoded, per Kronecker, as finite Hankel rank (finiteRank); laurentDynamicFunction is the series -sum M_n z^{-n-1}. Hankel columns c_j(h), their span K_Q, the sesquilinear Hankel form with [c_i(u), c_j(v)] = <u, M_{i+j} v> (hankelForm_single_single), its null space, the quotient state space with the descended form (hankelStateForm), A_Q c_j = c_{j+1} (hankelShift, well-defined by hankelFormalShift_null_le) and Gamma_Q h = c_0(h) (hankelSource). Proved in addition: the null space equals the kernel of the formal-to-literal column map for Hermitian coefficients (hankelNull_eq_ker), so the quotient is canonically the literal column span (hankelStateEquivColumnSpace), and [A^i Gamma u, A^j Gamma v] = <u, M_{i+j} v>. Not encoded: the equivalence rational-function <-> finite Hankel rank (Kronecker) and the identification of the tsum with the rational function.

thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein.title: Complete normalized rational generalized-Nevanlinna realization
thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein.note: Proved for Q encoded as in def:supp-rational-Hermitian (Hermitian Laurent coefficients M_n at infinity with finite Hankel rank; H finite dimensional). A finite Pontryagin realization (PontryaginRealization) is a finite-dimensional Hilbert majorant N with an invertible self-adjoint Gram operator J (form [x,y] = <x,Jy>; a fundamental symmetry J^2 = 1 is the special case of a suitably normalised majorant, and the negative index does not depend on the majorant), a J-self-adjoint state operator A and a source Gamma; output Gamma^+ = Gamma^* J, Markov parameters M_n = Gamma^* J A^n Gamma (Hermitian: markov_adjoint), transfer function Q(z) = Gamma^* J (A-z)^{-1} Gamma. The canonical construction (Hankel state space on its Euclidean carrier, Hankel form as Gram operator, shift A_Q, source Gamma_Q) is NormalizedRationalHermitianData.canonical with: canonical_markov (L_Q A_Q^n Gamma_Q = M_n); canonical_transfer_eq_toFun = eq:supp-rational-realization, Q(z) = Gamma_Q^+ (A_Q - z)^{-1} Gamma_Q, proved as an identity of functions on the region ||A_Q|| < |z| where the Laurent series defining Q converges (both sides are rational, so this is the paper's rational continuation; the resolvent Neumann series is the reusable Analysis/ResolventNeumannSeries.lean); finrank_carrier and mcMillanDegree_eq_finrank_columnSpace = eq:supp-rational-degree (dimension = stabilized Hankel rank = dim of the Hankel column span), with mcMillanDegree_le_realization (every linear realization L A^n Gamma = M_n has at least that dimension) and canonical_isCyclic (source minimality); canonical_form_eq / negIndex_canonical_form (the Pontryagin form is the Hankel form and the negative index is its inertia, negIndex = largest dimension of a negative definite subspace); negSquares_toFun_eq_negIndex: the Nevanlinna kernel N_Q(z,w) = (Q(z)-Q(w)^*)/(z - conj w) (eq:supp-Nevanlinna-kernel) has exactly negIndex negative squares (sup of the negative inertia of finite kernel Grams) on every upper half-plane neighbourhood of infinity {Im z > 0, |z| > rho}, rho >= ||A_Q||, and negSquares_canonical_transfer_eq on the whole upper half-plane part of the resolvent set of the realization; mechanism: inner_nevanlinnaKernel (kernel Gram = Pontryagin Gram of the resolvent-source vectors), negIndex_pullback_le (a compression cannot increase the index) and resolventSourceSpan_eq_top (resolvent-source span = power-cyclic span, via the limit -w(A-w)^{-1} -> 1). Uniqueness: PontryaginRealization.existsUnique_sourceFixing_unitary: any two source-cyclic finite Pontryagin realizations with the same Laurent coefficients are related by a unique linear isomorphism fixing the source, intertwining the state operators and preserving the indefinite forms (the source-fixing Pontryagin unitary). Scoped: 'minimal' is read as source-cyclic (the paper's source minimality; observability is automatic from nondegeneracy, futureRead_separating).

thm:supp-pole-Hankel.title: Pole--Hankel invariants
thm:supp-pole-Hankel.note: PROVED as NormalizedRationalHermitianData.poleHankelInvariants for the canonical minimal realization P = Q.canonical of a normalized rational Hermitian Q (its transfer function Gamma^+ (A - z)^{-1} Gamma is the rational continuation of Q, eq:supp-rational-realization). New infrastructure: Algebra/RootSubspaceProjection.lean (Riesz projection rootProj f mu onto the root subspace R_mu = maxGenEigenspace along the sum of the other root subspaces, for any endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space over an algebraically closed field: commutes with f, idempotent, (f - mu)^dim kills its range, and the regular pencil (f - mu)(1 - pi) + pi is invertible). Predictive/PoleHankelLocalRealization.lean: principal-part coefficients C_k = Gamma^* J (A - lam)^k pi_lam Gamma and the PRINCIPAL-PART DECOMPOSITION transfer_eq_principalPart_add_regularPart: for every z != lam in the resolvent set, Q(z) = -sum_{k < dim N} (z - lam)^{-k-1} C_k + R_lam(z), where R_lam(z) = Gamma^* J ((A - z)(1 - pi) + pi)^{-1} (1 - pi) Gamma is continuous at z = lam (continuousAt_regularPart), so the C_k are the principal part of Q at lam (for a non-pole lam they vanish). (P1) finrank_range_localHankelMap: local controllability (range_localCtrlMap) and observability (ker_localObsMap) of the local realization ((A - lam)|R_lam, pi_lam Gamma, Gamma^* J|R_lam) follow from source cyclicity and nondegeneracy, so rank [C_{i+j+s}]_{i,j < dim N} = rank ((A - lam)|R_lam)^s for every shift s; s = 0 gives the local McMillan degree dim R_lam; by NilpotentHankel.card_chains_ge_eq_finrank_sub the differences of these ranks are the numbers of Jordan chains of each length. (P2) at a real lam the Gram of the local Krylov family is the principal-part Hankel Gram [<e_k, C_{i+j} e_l>] (gram_localKrylov_of_real), so neg(R_lam) = negInertia, pos(R_lam) = posInertia (subNegIndex/subPosIndex_rootSpace_eq_..._localHankelGram) and neg + pos = dim R_lam (nondegeneracy). (P3), (P4) as before (subNegIndex_poleBlock_of_pos, negSquares_eq_sum_localIndex). Scoped/disclosed: 'pole' is rendered as an arbitrary point lam (the statements are trivial when R_lam = 0); the uniqueness of a principal-part decomposition (that C_k is determined by Q alone, a textbook Laurent fact) is not separately formalised; the Jordan block sizes are rendered as the rank sequence of the nilpotent local state operator, and the count lemma takes the existence of a Jordan chain basis as a hypothesis (not in Mathlib); the Hankel operators use blocks of size dim N (any size >= the nilpotency index works).

cor:supp-all-rational.title: All finite rational Hermitian dynamics
cor:supp-all-rational.note: PROVED (sorry-free, standard axioms only). New file Predictive/DescriptorWeierstrassForm.lean (1511 lines) closes the general (non-primary) side and assembles the corollary; bundled statement RenewalGeometry.cor_supp_all_rational. Setting: H, N finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces (the paper's finite setting); a regular Pontryagin descriptor realization is DescriptorRealization (E, A, Gamma, J) with regular pencil; a finite rational Hermitian dynamic function is FiniteRationalHermitianData Q = P + Q_0 (eq:supp-rational-split). (1) WEIERSTRASS REDUCTION: for any regular D and any real regular point t_0 (exists_real_regular), with T = E (A - t_0 E)^{-1}, pi_0 the Riesz projection onto the root subspace R_0 of T at 0 and W its root complement, the Weierstrass multiplier M = (1 + t_0 T) pi_0 + T (1 - pi_0) is an invertible J-self-adjoint operator commuting with T and pi_0 (weierstrassMul, isUnit_weierstrassMul, J_mul_weierstrassMul; pi_0 is J-self-adjoint, J_mul_rootProjL); the infinity block is the compression of (T M^{-1}, pi_0 Gamma, J M^{-1}) to R_0 (nilpotent, weierstrassInf_A_pow_finrank) and the finite block the compression of ((1 + t_0 T) M^{-1}, (1 - pi_0) Gamma, J M^{-1}) to W (PontryaginRealization.compress: compression of a Gram operator to a subspace on which its form is nondegenerate, compressGram_isUnit); D.weierstrassForm is the resulting PrimaryDescriptor and isSourceFixingUnitary_weierstrass verifies IsSourceFixingUnitary (D.rightMul (K M^{-1})) (D.weierstrassForm).toDescriptor S with S x = (pi_0 x, x - pi_0 x) (primaryEquiv), exactly as planned. weierstrassForm_transfer: the primary form has the same transfer function as D at every regular point (a source-fixing unitary preserves the transfer function, IsSourceFixingUnitary.transfer_eq). (2) MINIMALITY of general descriptor realizations: DescriptorRealization.IsMinimal := the resolvent-source vectors (A - zE)^{-1} Gamma h over the regular points z span the state space (the paper's source minimality of thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein). It is invariant under right multiplication (isMinimal_rightMul_iff) and source-fixing unitaries (IsSourceFixingUnitary.isMinimal, .symm), and on a primary form it is exactly PrimaryDescriptor.IsMinimal, i.e. both blocks source-cyclic (toDescriptor_isMinimal_iff; the Laurent/Vandermonde step is inlL_A_pow_Gamma_mem_resolventSourceSpan via coeff_eq_zero_of_tendsto_zero for the polynomial part and the real-ray resolvent limit Gamma_mem_resolventSourceSpan_real / resolventSourceSpan_realRay_eq_top for the strictly proper part). Hence D.IsMinimal <-> (D.weierstrassForm t_0).IsMinimal (isMinimal_iff_weierstrassForm_isMinimal). (3) THE EQUIVALENCE eq:supp-all-rational-equivalence: existence: Q.descriptor (primary direct sum of the infinity chain of P and the canonical realization of Q_0) is a minimal regular descriptor realization of Q (FiniteRationalHermitianData.descriptor_isMinimal, eventually_descriptor_transfer_eq_toFun); every minimal regular D realizes the finite rational Hermitian datum D.toData (eventually_toData_toFun_eq_transfer), whose coefficients are determined by the transfer function (toData_coeff_eq_of_transfer_eventuallyEq); uniqueness: a minimal D realizing Q is equivalent to Q.descriptor by reduction to Weierstrass primary form followed by a UNIQUE source-fixing descriptor Pontryagin unitary (existsUnique_sourceFixing_unitary_weierstrassForm_descriptor), and any two minimal realizations with the same dynamic function have Weierstrass forms related by a unique source-fixing unitary (existsUnique_sourceFixing_unitary_weierstrassForm). Dimension: every regular realization of Q has dim N >= McM(P) + McM(Q_0) (mcMillanDegree_add_le_finrank) and every minimal one has dim N = McM(P) + McM(Q_0) (finrank_eq_of_isMinimal): the minimal realizations attain the minimum state dimension. DISCLOSED RENDERINGS: (a) 'same dynamic function' is rendered as equality of transfer functions for all large real t (a neighbourhood of infinity on the real axis; rational functions agreeing there agree everywhere); (b) the paper's 'unique descriptor equivalence' between non-primary realizations is read as reduction to Weierstrass primary form (the right multiplication (E, A, Gamma, J) -> (EV, AV, Gamma, JV) by the J-self-adjoint unit V = (A - t_0 E)^{-1} M^{-1}, which preserves the transfer function, followed by the source-fixing unitary x -> (pi_0 x, x - pi_0 x)) followed by the unique source-fixing unitary between the primary forms; the primary form and D.toData depend on the chosen real regular point t_0, but the Laurent coefficients do not; (c) the negative-index part of 'attains both minimum ... indices' is not formalised here (the index statements are the separately ledgered thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein / thm:supp-pole-Hankel results); (d) minimality is source minimality (resolvent-source span = whole space), as in the paper's proof of thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein.

thm:supp-common-source.title: Joint Gram classification
thm:supp-common-source.note: Proved in finite dimensions with E_a = C^{n a} (index types in Type, as required by the reused repo lemma source_kernel_realization_minimal_unique) and X = Sigma a, n a. Corr_X = {K psd, K_aa = I} (CorrelationSpectrahedron); G_X = Pi_a U(n a) acting by block congruence K -> D(g)^H K D(g) (gaugeAct), which preserves Corr_X (block_gaugeAct, gaugeAct_mem_corr); Stab(K) is a Subgroup (stabilizer). A joint realization of K on a common space C^C is S : Matrix C X with S^H S = K (columns over block a = images of the marginal basis), its realization space Ran S. Proved: the Gram of a realization lies in Corr_X iff its marginal blocks are identities (isometric V_a); every K in Corr_X is realized (by sqrt K) with rank = rank K; every realization's Ran S has dimension exactly rank K and rank K <= dim of the common space (rank K is the minimum joint realization dimension, attained by restricting to Ran S); two realizations are equivalent up to a marginal frame change g and a source-fixing isometric identification of the realization spaces iff their Grams lie in the same G_X-orbit (frameUnitaryEquivalent_iff; the identification is unique, exists_unique_range_unitary, via the repo's joint_source_unique_range_unitary); for a realization S of K, a frame change g is implemented by such a unitary on Ran S iff g in Stab(K) (mem_stabilizer_iff_residual). Modelling disclosure: 'unitary on the common realization space' is formalised as a source-fixing linear equivalence between the ranges preserving the ambient inner product (the repo's convention), and 'minimal' as restriction to Ran S.

cth:supp-pairwise-not-global.title: Pairwise positivity need not give a joint realization
cth:supp-pairwise-not-global.note: The explicit 3×3 real matrix M = !![1,-3/4,-3/4; -3/4,1,-3/4; -3/4,-3/4,1]: M *ᵥ (1,1,1) = (-1/2)•(1,1,1), hence Module.End.HasEigenvalue (Matrix.toLin' M) (-1/2); M is not Matrix.PosSemidef (quadratic form -3/2 on (1,1,1)); and for every i ≠ j in Fin 3 the principal block M.submatrix ![i,j] ![i,j] is Matrix.PosDef (all blocks equal !![1,-3/4;-3/4,1], whose form is (x₀ - 3x₁/4)² + 7x₁²/16). So pairwise-admissible Gram blocks need not assemble into a positive joint Gram operator.

thm:supp-finite-exhaustion.title: Finite stratified fibre in the fully reduced coordinate model
thm:supp-finite-exhaustion.note: Proved in the reformulation the paper's proof establishes. A fully reduced finite realization of the completed target is rendered by its retained data (FullyReducedRealization): a joint Gram point K in Corr_X (thm:supp-common-source, JointGram.CorrelationSpectrahedron) together with points of the five retained fibres J_X x M_X x P_X x C_X^cal x R_X, which enter as sets with an action of the gauge group G_X = Prod_a U(E_a); the gauge group acts on Corr_X by the block congruence of thm:supp-common-source (instMulActionGaugeGroupCorr; gaugeAct is a right action, composed with inversion to a left action with the same orbits, mem_orbit_iff_gaugeAct, and the same stabilizers, which are the residual gauge groups Stab_{G_X}(K) of thm:supp-common-source, mem_stabilizer_iff_jointGram). Real_X^{sharp,min}(S) is defined as the set of fully reduced realizations modulo simultaneous gauge equivalence (RealizationSpace, the orbit space).
